name: Pullman estate (1800 S. Calumet Avenue): the two-storey stone lodge between the glasshouse ranges

function.note: The 1911 sheet letters it 'D', a dwelling, at the angle of the two glasshouse ranges; the sheet-28 census reads it as the estate's gardener's lodge (s28-pullman-garden-lodge, tier reconstructed): nothing names its occupant or use beyond the 1911 'D'.

research_note: T-3164 (piece 1 of T-1934): built on the district draft's builder (generators/archetypes/prairie_draft.py) because no kit carries a small service dwelling yet, and exempt from the draft rules' re-derivation because the rules' skip names it (as T-2538 did for 1801). Read off sheet 28 by hand: the colour trace would follow this copy's pink wash, which runs diagonally into the east glasshouse range rather than stopping at the lodge's dashed east line. Heights, roof and openings are the draft rules' brick-family values (L-pullman-glasshouses-1800-calumet-3164). T-3165 refines it to the pictures. T-3164 re-entered (2026-10-28): rebuilt to the 1894 Inland plate's north front, in stone under a crested deck roof; see draft_elevation's note for what the plate still shows that this does not.

documented_range.note: The record claims the 1904 target and no more: the 1911 sheet draws the building and the sheet-28 census (chicago/prairie_1904_v1/data/sheet_census/sheet-28.json, allocation s28-pullman-service-garden) rules the Pullman estate's glasshouse ground and its lodge present in 1904. Its building date, which the census reads off the 1894 conservatory plate, is T-3165's to read from the pictures themselves.

position.note: The north-east corner, read off the committed sheet 28 raster at pixel (3186, 2359) where the drawn wall lines cross, and carried to the local frame by the sheet's fitted similarity (data/traces/gcp/sanborn_1911_v3_sheet_28_gcps.json; 1.47 m RMS on independent standing houses): local E 1470.53, N -3274.69. The bearing turns the plan onto the sheet's own ruled lines (1.014 degrees off east in that fit), so u runs west to the alley and v south, and the building runs square to the lot as drawn.

derivation.reason: The four derivation methods re-derive from the 1835 files; none reads a 1911 Sanborn sheet. This position is the pixel named in the note, of the committed sheet 28 raster, carried through the similarity in data/traces/gcp/sanborn_1911_v3_sheet_28_gcps.json (local_e = a*px + b*py + c, local_n = d*px + e*py + f) plus the datum origin, so the sum can be recomputed by hand.

footprint.note: u from the east wall west to the alley, v from the north wall south. The drawn lines' centres on the sheet (x 3009-3186, y 2359-2588) at 0.0506 m a pixel: 8.95 by 11.58 m. Its north wall is the north range's south end and its east wall the east range's west end, as the sheet draws them.

stories.note: The sheet prints '2' on the lodge: two storeys.

construction.note: T-3164 re-entered: the 1894 Inland plate shows the lodge's north front in coursed rock-faced stone like the east range it adjoins, not brick; the 1911 sheet's pink wash in its north-west corner is read as the colourist's, as its diagonal run into the glasshouse already was. The sheet's '2' stands.

parts.from: the sheet's lodge outline, read by hand (T-3164); its roof the plate's: a steep hip cut off at a crested lead deck

the front's west part, which the 1894 Inland plate and Lowe's print both draw with its own lower hipped roof and quoined east return (T-3164): its face on the sheet's north wall, where the north range abuts it, 4.85 m wide from the loggia's west end at u 4.1

draft_plan.note: Two rectangles (T-3164, west part pass). The sheet draws one outline, 8.95 by 11.58 m, and no wing or bay on it; the 1894 Inland plate and Lowe's print (c. 1897) both draw the north front in two parts. The west part, from the loggia's west end (u 4.1, the plate's x 1052, Lowe's 662) to the west wall, stands proud of the loggia block with a quoined east return, its eave a few pixels over the block's in both pictures, and carries its own hipped roof, whose north-east hip rises from the return to about the deck's height (plate x 1058,712 to 1118,625). The return's width and the eave's step both read about 2 m of projection through the solved cameras. The part's face is put on the sheet's north wall, where the north range abuts it, and the loggia block is set 2 m back behind it, rather than the part 2 m out over the range: the pictures fix the step, not which face the sheet's line is, and this way the 1904 range meets masonry the sheet draws. The block's corner then reads x 940 on the plate and 576 on Lowe's print, where both draw it (they were 947 and 582). Its depth behind the front (6.0 m) and its ridge (11.75 m at the main roof's 52 degrees) are RECONSTRUCTED; the pictures see only its north and east slopes (L-pullman-lodge-west-part-3164). T-3164 re-entered: the roof is the plate's, a steep hip (about 52 degrees) stopped at a flat deck 3.7 m over the eave inside an iron cresting, the deck's north edge reading x 1010-1105 on the plate (2.8 m in from the east eave, 3.1 m from the west); the deck's depth is reconstructed at the same pitch.

draft_elevation.note: T-3164 RE-ENTERED against the 1894 Inland plate (data/reference_views/pullman_glasshouse_1800_calumet_pavilion/inland_1894_conservatory.json; 25.8 px/m at the lodge, grade y 931, its north-east corner at x 948, 25.5 px/m along the front): the north front is a tall ground storey, a loggia of three openings between round columns (dark x 955-967, 977-1003 and 1015-1052, so 0.5, 1.0 and 1.45 m wide at 0.51, 1.65 and 3.35 m west of the east wall, the columns between them about 0.45 m) under an entablature whose underside reads y 812 (4.6 m); a balcony band y 775-795 (5.3-6.0 m) across it; one small upper sash over the middle opening, x 998-1017 and y 751-773 (0.75 m wide, 6.1-7.0 m); and the eave at y 720 (8.2 m), so storeys of 5.5 and 2.7 m over grade. The plate shows no stack on the slopes it sees; the Lowe photograph (c. 1897) shows one rising behind the east slope, so the draft's stack (which the rules had stood on the north-west, in the plate's view) is moved there, 2.4 m in from the east wall and 8 m back, its top 11.8 m (the print's stack top about 15 px under the deck's cresting), its place behind the slope RECONSTRUCTED. T-3164 (third pass): the upper storey's north-east corner turned on a bow (a 1.2 m chord along each wall, 0.1 m proud of the corner, 5.3-8.2 m) with the eave carried round it and belled 0.4 m out and down (the roof's bowed chamfer); a balcony on the loggia's entablature, its floor at 5.3 m and an open balustrade 0.75 m high, 0.45 m deep from 0.2 m east of the corner to 4.2 m along the front, its east end turned on a quarter-round under the bow; two round columns 0.38 m across between the loggia's openings; and the deck in the stable's open cresting with a spire at each corner, as the plate shows them (L-pullman-lodge-front-3164: the bow's plan, the balcony's depth and balusters, the columns' bases and capitals and the cresting's pattern are RECONSTRUCTED). T-3164 (west part pass): the front's west part is built with its own lower hipped roof, see draft_plan; STILL OPEN against the plate: a dark pointed form over that roof at x 1120-1135, a finial or a stack too small to read. UNRESOLVED: neither the plate nor the Lowe photograph shows the lodge's east face or east slope over the east range's coping (both show sky and a railing there), which the sheet's 11.6 m-deep two-storey outline and the two solved cameras, both standing east of the lodge, say should show; either the two-storey block is shallower than the sheet draws or the cameras stand further west than solved, and this record keeps the sheet's outline until that is read. RECONSTRUCTED: the west and south fronts, which no picture shows, keep the draft rules' sash and the south door (L-pullman-glasshouses-1800-calumet-3164). WHAT T-3164 FIRST BUILT: RECONSTRUCTED on the draft rules' brick-family values: a hipped roof over two storeys, three bays on its alley front with the door at the south end, one stack, no dormers. Nothing describes the lodge beyond the sheet's '2' and 'D' (L-pullman-glasshouses-1800-calumet-3164).
